newsitem.title: USA: Marriott sees distribution services growth.
newsitem.headline: Marriott sees distribution services growth.

text.p: Marriott International Inc sees external revenues for its food service distribution arm doubling in 1997 from 1996 levels, said Michael Stein, the chief financial officer.
"External revenues from the distribution business are expected to double in 1997," he said, at a Montgomery Securities Hospitality conference in New York.

Stein declined to comment on specific numbers, but a chart distributed by the company showed total revenue forecasts for 1996 at around $1.2 billion for Marriott Distribution Services. The chart showed total distribution services revenue for 1997 at around $1.7 billion, of which external revenue were forecast to be around two-thirds of total revenue.
Stein said the company is set to announce its fourth quarter and year end results later this week.

He also said the company continues to target annual percentage increases at a high teen rate. He said that acquisitions would remain a priority for Marriott, and that the company had spent nearly $1 billion in acquisitions over the last 24 months.
"We expect acquisitions to continue as an integral part of our strategy," he said.
In the hotel sector, Stein said the company had set a goal of adding about 120,000 rooms world-wide by the year 2001, of which about 25,000 rooms were slated for markets outside the United States.
